caption: The drawing depicts an old stone doorway that has been sealed with bricks and stones. The arch of the doorway is constructed from large, pale gray blocks that form a rounded arch shape with visible seams and some minor carvings or details on the stones near the keystone. Flanking the doorway on both sides are vertical stone elements with linear decorative designs carved into them. The doorway itself is completely blocked by a rough wall composed of darker, irregularly shaped stones and a portion of reddish-brown brickwork visible near the top center. The surrounding wall is made up of a mix of light gray, tan, and beige stones, giving a textured, uneven appearance. The drawing has a soft, muted color palette dominated by shades of gray, tan, brown, and touches of red. The composition is centered on the doorway, with the details of the surrounding stonework also included. The artist’s signature, “Juanita Boixhoss,” appears near the lower right corner.
title: Doorway, Stone
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
